summary:
I merged the five M2 planner outputs, the toolchain scout report and the API gap audit into one task graph: 90 tasks (E1 21, E2 20, E3 21, E5 17, E4 11; 26 opus, 63 sonnet, 1 haiku). The graph is acyclic, has a critical path of 12 tasks, and is laid out in 20 waves with at most 5 tasks per wave.

**Duplicates removed**
- **"Show the equivalent `forge` command".** There were three designs. One remains: a `cli_template` column in the API method table, rendered identically in Rust (E1-T4) and TS (E1-T13), plus an action registry. E4-T5 checks coverage with an allowlist of CLI-only commands.
- **GUI data layer.** There were three. One remains: E1-T9. Sparklines and the status bar poll `services.status` every 2 s while visible; the persisted `service.metrics` events are not used.
- **Fake daemon and test harness.** There were four. One remains: fakeBridge (E1-T8) plus the scenario library, Playwright and real-window tooling (E1-T19).
- **Daemon auto-start and connection state.** These move into forge-ipc (E1-T2).
- **Opening files and URLs (ShellExecute).** Implemented once in forge-core (E1-T3) and reused by E3.
- **Access-log parsing.** One parser in forge-metrics (E5-T3), reused by the Logs `site:` target (E3-T8).

**Gaps the audit raised, now covered**
- A real bug in the shipped M1 CLI: `forge logs -f` can drop live lines after a daemon restart or log rotation (sequence numbers restart). Fixed in E2-T2, scheduled in wave 2. This fixes develop only; whether to ship a 0.1.1 hotfix is your call.
- Serialized config writes, plus a `config.changed` event (E3-T10).
- The port-conflict payload names the owner by internal id instead of `mysql/default` (E1-T3).
- Structured error details, so the GUI can show cause plus action in pt-BR/en-US (E1-T3).
- A `tls.list` method, needed to warn about expiring site certificates (E2-T1, E2-T6).
- `forge tls ca uninstall`, already a known issue in 0.1.0 (E3-T11).

**Screen items no planner covered, now added**
- Serviços "Avançado" tab, instance data dir and same-series version change (E2-T10).
- The "Encerrar" action for a foreign process holding a port (E3-T11, E3-T19).
- The site "Ambiente" tab with masked secrets (E3-T20).
- The site "Banco" tab (E3-T14).
- Xdebug IDE key (E2-T9).
- Unread mail count in the tray (E3-T13).
- Settings screen to rebind shortcuts (E3-T16).
- Performance alerts in the Dashboard "Atenção" area (E5-T17).

**Numbering**
- ADR-0033 is already taken on release/0.1.0, so M2 uses ADR-0034 to 0045, with 0046 to 0049 as spares.
- New database migrations take the next free number at rebase time (0004, 0005).
- `API_VERSION` goes to 1.1 exactly once for all of M2 (E1-T3 merges first).

**Before and during the work**
- M2 must not start before release/0.1.0 is merged back into develop.
- The cold-start and metrics performance measurements (E1-T21, E5-T13) need a quiet machine. Pause other builds while they run.
- The M2 gate needs you for a short in-person section: real vibrancy at the physical console (your session is RDP), Win11-only checks, real DPI scaling, tray and toasts, then your sign-off.

**Decisions for you**
1. Whether the app updater is active in 0.2.0. If it ships active, its signing key can never change.
2. Approval to update CLAUDE.md. Agents will not edit it on their own.
3. Whether to ship a 0.1.1 hotfix for the `forge logs -f` bug.

**Fallback plans used**
- No GitHub push: CI is validated locally plus actionlint.
- No pixel-diff screenshot gate in M2: screenshots are artifacts, plus a size-capped reference set in `docs/design/screens`.
- No tauri-driver: real-window tests attach over WebView2 CDP and capture the frame with PrintWindow.
env_recipe:
Scope and safety:
- Work only in your own worktree on feature/<ID>-<slug>, branched from develop AFTER the release/0.1.0 merge-back.
- Never touch C:/apps_src/Forgebox (main tree), the REL/E1 worktrees, or C:/laragon. Reading/executing node from C:/laragon/bin/nodejs/node-v24 is the only exception.
- Never push.
- Never change the global PATH, the global npm/pnpm config, ~/.npmrc, the registry, or system installs. If something must be installed system-wide, stop and report it.

Node: prepend C:/laragon/bin/nodejs/node-v24 to YOUR process PATH only.
- bash: export PATH="/c/laragon/bin/nodejs/node-v24:$PATH"
- PowerShell: $env:Path = 'C:\laragon\bin\nodejs\node-v24;' + $env:Path
This gives node 24.22.1; do NOT use C:/Program Files/node-20. pnpm 10.7.1 comes from scoop. Verify with `node -v` and `pnpm -v` before work.

TLS: the registry works today without extra config. If TLS errors appear, set NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca in your own process env only.
- Never add a project .npmrc with strict-ssl=false.
- The project must not rely on the user's ~/.npmrc.
- For Rust/git, keep the existing schannel config.

Pinned frontend stack (from the M2 spike): react/react-dom 19.3.1, vite 8.3.5, @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.2, tailwindcss + @tailwindcss/vite 4.3.3, @tauri-apps/api 2.12.4, @tauri-apps/cli 2.12.4 (devDependency), @playwright/test 1.64.1, radix-ui 1.8.1, motion 14.7.1.
- TypeScript: pin the newest 5.x/6.x line supported by typescript-eslint (decision in E1-T1), not 7.0 native.
- Crates: tauri 2 (2.12.x), tauri-build 2, window-vibrancy 0.8. Never tauri 3 alpha.
- Set package.json packageManager to pnpm@10.7.1 and engines.node >= 24.
- pnpm 10 blocks lifecycle scripts: list the needed ones in pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies.

Tauri CLI: always use the pinned npm CLI (`pnpm -C apps/desktop tauri dev|build|icon`), never the system cargo-tauri 2.4.
- Icons: `pnpm tauri icon <512px png>`; icons/icon.ico is required.
- Tailwind: restrict sources (`@import "tailwindcss" source("./")` or `@source not "../src-tauri"`) so src-tauri/target is not scanned.

Rust: `cargo build|clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings|test --workspace` must keep working WITHOUT Node and without apps/desktop/dist (E1-T1 guarantee).
- The cold debug build of src-tauri takes about 3 min.
- Expect 2-4x slower builds while other worktrees compile.

Window startup: visible:false, transparent:true, decorations:false. Show the window from the `ready` command after a double requestAnimationFrame that follows the first React commit.
- Render the shell first; connect to the daemon after first paint. Never block first paint on the daemon.
- Lazy-load routes; keep the initial JS <= ~70 kB gzip.

Vibrancy:
- Decide the effect from forge-core SystemAppearance (OS build >= 22000 means Mica; RDP, EnableTransparency=0, high contrast or prefers-reduced-transparency mean opaque) and from window_vibrancy's Result. Tauri set_effects returns Ok on Win10 while doing nothing.
- Without an effect the transparent area renders black, so the fallback must paint an opaque --bg-sidebar.
- This user's session is RDP, so the expected automatic state here is data-vibrancy=off.

Unit tests: `pnpm -C apps/desktop test` (vitest + Testing Library + jsdom).

Web UI tests: Playwright with channel 'msedge' (installed Edge 156; set PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1) against `vite build --mode qa && vite preview`, using the fakeBridge scenarios (?scenario=empty|populated|heavy|errors|not-implemented|daemon-down|slow|remote, plus theme/vibrancy/motion/locale params).
- Commands: `pnpm e2e`, `pnpm qa:shots`, `pnpm qa:check`, `pnpm qa:perf`.
- If Edge cannot be used, the fallback is chromium-headless-shell with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH pointing to a project-local folder.

Real Tauri window tests:
- Start the debug or release Forgebox.exe with WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=<free port> (test env only, never in code or release config) and FORGE_GUI_DATA_DIR=<temp>.
- Then call chromium.connectOverCDP('http://127.0.0.1:<port>'); the page is http://tauri.localhost/.
- For the native frame (titlebar/material), use scripts/qa/capture-window.ps1 (PrintWindow PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT). CopyFromScreen fails on this RDP session.
- Do not use tauri-driver/msedgedriver.

PowerShell scripts: run with `powershell -NoProfile -File <script>`. Do NOT pass -ExecutionPolicy Bypass (auto-mode denies it); the CurrentUser policy is RemoteSigned.

Look at screenshots with the Read tool. Prefer the per-screen contact sheets in apps/desktop/qa/out/<run>/; qa/out is gitignored.

Live and online tests:
- Use temp portable roots under %TEMP% (FORGEBOX_ROOT / portable.flag pattern from crates/forge-cli/tests/common) with DNS off and fake binaries.
- Reuse the cached zips in C:/apps_src/Forgebox-wt/cache read-only. Extract to temp, never into the cache.
- Laragon may hold ports 80/443/3306; tests must allocate free ports.
- Never write to HKCU Run, the cert stores or NRPT in automated tests; inject fake backends.
- Teardown must leave no forgeboxd, Forgebox.exe or msedgewebview2 process behind.

Registry signing: tasks that change registry/ run `cargo xtask registry-index` and `cargo xtask registry-sign --key C:/apps_src/Forgebox-wt/cache/keys/dev.key`.
- The key is read-only; never copy or commit it.
- On rebase, regenerate and re-sign index.yaml; never hand-merge it.

Generated files (apps/desktop/src/ipc/generated.ts, methods.ts, registry/schema/*.json, registry/index.yaml(.minisig)): on any rebase conflict, take develop's version, then rerun `cargo xtask gen-ts` / `cargo xtask schema` / registry-index+sign, and commit.
- CI drift checks must pass.
- Every new METHODS row needs a cli_template (or an empty cli) plus its clap stub in the same PR, so the coverage tests stay green.

Numbering at merge time:
- ADRs: M2 uses ADR-0034..0049 with the assignment given in each task. Before merging, re-check docs/adr/README.md on develop and renumber on collision.
- SQL migrations: take the next free number when you rebase, and never edit a merged migration.
- API_VERSION: bumped to 1.1 exactly once in M2 (by the first contract PR to merge); later PRs keep 1.1.

Repo conventions:
- Commits: `M2-E<n>-T<n>: short description`, ending with the Co-Authored-By line from the harness.
- One PR per task, with tests. Update the docs you diverge from in the same PR.
- UI text: pt-BR + en-US. Identifiers, logs and commits: English.
- Do not edit CLAUDE.md. Propose changes in the PR description instead; the user must approve them.

Quiet-machine rule: cold-start (E1-T21, M2 gate) and metrics CPU/p99 measurements (E5-T13) only run when no other worktree is compiling. The orchestrator schedules a quiet slot. Report the median of the runs and the session type.
blockers: Hard prerequisite: release/0.1.0 must be finished and merged back into develop before any M2 branch is created. It changes generated.ts (DnsMode/DnsPolicyReason), net.dns_status and adds ADR-0033, which onboarding, Dashboard and DNS settings rely on. Wave 1 starts only after the merge-back.

No push access: the GitHub Actions changes (desktop job, desktop-release job) can only be validated locally (scripts/ci.ps1 -Desktop) and with actionlint. actionlint is not known to be installed. If it is missing, install it into a local tools dir (e.g. C:/apps_src/Forgebox-wt/cache/tools) and never system-wide; report it if that fails.

Human-only verification (the M2 gate cannot close without the user):
- The session is RDP, so real Acrylic blur, frame pacing during resize, global hotkeys and native screen capture need the physical console.
- No Win11 machine is available for Mica, snap layouts or Segoe UI Variable.
- Native toasts need an installed release build.
- Real DPI scaling and multi-monitor DPI need manual Windows settings changes.

oha (M2-E5-T13 load generator) is not installed. Plan: `cargo install oha --locked --root C:/apps_src/Forgebox-wt/cache/tools` (not system-wide). If corporate TLS blocks it, stop and ask the user before replacing it with an in-repo load generator, because that changes how the acceptance is measured.
The dev registry signing key must exist at C:/apps_src/Forgebox-wt/cache/keys/dev.key (read-only) for E2-T3, E3-T2, E5-T2 and E5-T12. Without it the index cannot be re-signed.

Quiet-machine windows: E1-T21 (cold start) and E5-T13 (daemon CPU/p99) give invalid numbers while other worktrees compile (2-4x distortion measured in the spike). The orchestrator must pause or serialize builds during those steps.

Cold-start budget headroom is only ~150-250 ms (spike: release median 627 ms; WebView2 init alone 420-540 ms; debug builds cannot pass). Any synchronous daemon wait, large initial bundle or eager route import will break the gate.
Optional: the PostgreSQL zip in the cache is not confirmed. The ignored online tests of E3-T5/E3-T6 need it, or they stay ignored with a note.

decisions_for_user.question: Should the app updater (tauri-plugin-updater, docs/05 §5) be ACTIVE in the 0.2.0 release? A shipped updater public key cannot be rotated without a release signed by the old key. docs/05 (github.com/forgebox/forgebox) and Cargo.toml (github.com/deverity/Forgebox) also disagree on the repository, and the production signing key is an M4-E1 topic.
options: A) Compile the updater in, but leave it inactive in 0.2.0: no production pubkey and no endpoint. The UI shows 'atualizações do app chegam na versão 1.0' and only dev/test builds get a dev key plus a FORGEBOX_UPDATER_ENDPOINT override.
B) Activate it in 0.2.0: you choose the canonical repository URL now and generate and safeguard the production minisign key before the release.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: A. It keeps the irreversible key and endpoint choice for M4-E1, when signing and the installer are designed, and M2 loses nothing testable. E1-T18 implements the whole flow (check, verify, daemon.stop handoff, passive install) behind configuration, and its tests use a local server and the dev key.

decisions_for_user.question: May agents update CLAUDE.md at the end of M2? Two changes are proposed. (1) Commands: add pnpm -C apps/desktop test|e2e|qa:check|qa:shots|perf:startup and scripts/ci.ps1 -Desktop. (2) Clarify the Win32 rule: GUI window presentation may use window-vibrancy and Tauri plugins in src-tauri, but there is no direct windows/windows-sys dependency there, and OS facts go through forge-core traits re-exported by forge_ipc::base.
options: Approve both edits in the M2 gate PR
Keep CLAUDE.md unchanged; ADR-0035 and docs carry the clarification
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Approve both in the gate PR. This is not irreversible, but CLAUDE.md is protected: agents will not edit it without your explicit approval. Until then ADR-0035, docs/02 and apps/desktop/README.md carry the information, and the E1-T1 architecture guard enforces the rule mechanically.

decisions_for_user.question: The logs.subscribe sequence bug also affects the shipped 0.1.0 CLI. `forge logs -f` can silently drop live lines after a daemon restart or a log rotation. M2-E2-T2 fixes it on develop in wave 2. Should it also ship as a 0.1.1 hotfix?
options: Fix only on develop and ship it in 0.2.0
After v0.1.0 is tagged, cherry-pick the E2-T2 fix into hotfix/0.1.1 from main and release 0.1.1
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Release 0.1.1 after v0.1.0 is tagged. The fix is self-contained in crates/forge-daemon/src/api/logs.rs plus tests, and the bug makes the CLI's main debugging command unreliable. Nothing touches release/0.1.0 or the REL worktree while they are in use.

decisions_taken.question: Tauri bridge shape
decisions_taken.decision: Generic Tauri commands: ipc_call(context, method, params, request_id, timeout_ms) maps to Client::call_raw after validation against METHODS. ipc_subscribe uses a Tauri Channel, with frames batched to <= 16 ms or <= 256 items and explicit lagged/reset markers. The ipc token never reaches JS. No per-method Rust code. Trade-off: the webview can call any method its role allows, mitigated by bundled-only content, a strict CSP and capabilities limited to the main window.

decisions_taken.question: Who owns live state for the tray, and where do GUI-only prefs and state live
decisions_taken.decision: A Rust TrayModel actor with its own events.subscribe through the shared Contexts, so it keeps working while the webview is hidden. The snapshot state duplicated between Rust and TS is accepted. GUI prefs and state (theme, language, close-to-tray, shortcuts, muted notifications, window state, onboarding progress keyed per root/context, WebView2 profile) live client-side in %LOCALAPPDATA%/Forgebox/gui, or in <root>/state/gui in portable mode, with a FORGE_GUI_DATA_DIR override for tests. They are never stored in the daemon's forgebox.toml. This unifies the E1, E2 and E3 proposals.

decisions_taken.question: Daemon auto-start from the GUI
decisions_taken.decision: Same code as the CLI, moved into forge_ipc::client::local (E1-T2). The GUI starts the daemon only if the root is initialized; otherwise it routes to onboarding. After an unexpected loss it auto-restarts at most once per 60 s with backoff, and never after daemon.shutdown{reason:user}. Mutex exit code 4 counts as success. Only the 'Local' context exists in M2; loading remote profiles is M6.

decisions_taken.question: Win32 boundary for the GUI and the window material policy
decisions_taken.decision: src-tauri has no direct windows or windows-sys dependency, enforced by the E1-T1 architecture guard. window-vibrancy and Tauri plugins are allowed because docs/07 §2.3 and docs/02 already name them. OS facts (build, RDP, transparency setting, high contrast, accent colour, taskbar theme, process creation time) come from a new forge-core SystemAppearance trait re-exported via forge_ipc::base::platform, following the spawn_detached precedent of ADR-0030. The effect decision uses that snapshot together with window_vibrancy's Result, never Tauri's set_effects. Win11 gets Mica. Win10 is decided by measurement in E1-T7: opaque by default with an Acrylic opt-in if resize/drag frame pacing degrades. RDP, transparency off, high contrast or the user switch force opaque. Snap layouts get a time-boxed spike using a plugin only, with no Win32 of our own.

decisions_taken.question: How the equivalent forge command is produced and kept correct (three competing designs)
decisions_taken.decision: A cli_template column in the api_methods! table, rendered by MethodInfo::render_cli in Rust and by the TS renderer from methods.ts. A shared golden JSON is checked by both renderers, and a forge-cli clap round-trip test (try_parse_from maps back to the same method) validates the strings. GUI actions go through a mandatory defineAction registry, with an ESLint rule against direct mutating calls. E4-T5 checks coverage against cli-only.yaml, where every entry needs a reason. Open-in-editor, browser and folder actions are a documented exception: they show the underlying program command. E2's hand-written toCli design was dropped.

decisions_taken.question: Frontend test strategy and visual QA (E1 wanted committed CI baselines; E4 wanted no pixel gate)
decisions_taken.decision: vitest + Testing Library for units. Playwright on the msedge channel against a qa-mode Vite build with the single scenario-driven fakeBridge (which absorbs E4's FixtureTransport and E2's mock daemon) for screenshots, axe, keyboard, CLS, motion and perf checks. Real-window e2e attaches over WebView2 CDP via an env var used in tests only, and the native frame is captured with PrintWindow. No tauri-driver. No pixel-diff gate in M2, because font rendering differs between RDP and CI and baselines could not be produced on CI without push: shots are artifacts, plus a curated docs/design/screens set (<= 250 KB each, <= 8 MB total). Revisit pixel diff in M4.

decisions_taken.question: Cold-start definition
decisions_taken.decision: Release Forgebox.exe on this Win10 19045 machine with a warm WebView2 profile and no Forgebox GUI running. Measured from OS process creation time (or t0 just before spawn) to the `ready` command, which fires after a double requestAnimationFrame following the first shell commit; the window is shown at that point. One discarded warm-up plus 10 runs; the median must be < 800 ms with the daemon running and with it stopped, and p90/p95 are recorded. Runs only in a quiet machine window. CI reports the number and asserts only 1.5x the budget.

decisions_taken.question: Frontend libraries and tooling not fixed by docs
decisions_taken.decision: TanStack Router (code-based, one route file per feature), Zustand and TanStack Query (all named in docs/02). i18next + react-i18next with one namespace file per feature and locale, a key-parity test, a pseudo-locale in qa mode, and Rust include_str! of the tray and notifications namespaces. ESLint 9 flat config + typescript-eslint + react-hooks + jsx-a11y + eslint-plugin-i18next + a no-color-literals rule, plus stylelint and Prettier. TypeScript is pinned to the newest 5.x/6.x line that typescript-eslint supports, not 7.0 native. Design tokens are DTCG JSON in docs/design/tokens.json with a tiny generator and a drift check. Inter and JetBrains Mono come from @fontsource and tray .ico files use include_bytes! (docs/07 §7 and docs/08 updated). Charts use uPlot. cmdk for the palette, @tanstack/react-virtual for lists, xterm.js for the terminal. The /__gallery route replaces Storybook.
decisions_taken.adr_in_task: ADR-0034 (stack section) in M2-E1-T8; tokens in M2-E1-T6

decisions_taken.question: Data for CPU/RAM sparklines and the status bar (E1 wanted service.metrics events, E2 polling, the audit a new stream)
decisions_taken.decision: Poll services.status every 2 s only while a consuming view is mounted, visible and focused, keeping a 30-sample (60 s) ring per instance or pool on the client. Pool req/s comes from requests_total deltas. docs/03 §8 allows polling for metrics. The persisted service.metrics events stay off, because they would flood the 50k-event resume ring. No new stream in M2. The status bar shows daemon cpu/rss (DaemonStatusDto, added by E1-T3) plus the stack total; docs/07 §4 is clarified accordingly.

decisions_taken.question: How the API grows in M2 (several contract-first PRs touching the same files)
decisions_taken.decision: One contract-first PR per epic: E1-T3 (shell gaps), E3-T1, E2-T1 and E5-T1. All changes are additive, and API_VERSION is bumped to 1.1 exactly once by whichever merges first. New methods are registered in NOT_IMPLEMENTED with their task id, together with clap stubs and a cli_template. They merge serially, with gen-ts rerun after each rebase. API names are only treated as frozen at the v0.2.0 tag. Structured ApiError.details (reason, args) and CheckDto codes let the GUI localize from code plus details, never from the English message.
decisions_taken.adr_in_task: ADR-0039 in M2-E1-T3; ADR-0040 in M2-E3-T1; ADR-0041 in M2-E2-T1; ADR-0044 in M2-E5-T1

decisions_taken.question: Quick settings storage and writes
decisions_taken.decision: SQLite is the source of truth: instances.settings for instances, and a per-(tool, series) table in a new migration for PHP pools. Values are written only inside managed blocks with format-aware writers. PHP values go into a fully managed conf.d/90-forgebox-settings.ini overlay, so the user's php.ini is never edited. Reserved keys `ports.<name>` give 'Trocar porta'. apply=reload recycles the pool and apply=restart goes through the supervisor.

decisions_taken.question: Installing kind: Extension tools (Xdebug)
decisions_taken.decision: Generic and driven by manifest compat/variants against installed target versions (`--for php@X`, defaulting to every compatible version). The target link is stored in the tool_versions variant map, with no new migration. php.xdebug installs a missing extension inside its own job; the GUI confirms first. The IDE key is manifest quick-setting data.

decisions_taken.question: Instance advanced settings and port-conflict 'Encerrar' (E2 deferred them, the audit asked for them, docs/07 §1.2/§5.3 list them)
decisions_taken.decision: Both are in M2. services.update (autostart, args, env, restart policy, version change within the same series only) plus data_dir on create, in E2-T10. services.kill_port_holder (local_only, Admin, confirm=true; re-checks that the pid still holds the port, refuses Forgebox, system and critical processes, emits an audit event, TerminateProcess through forge-core) in E3-T11. Its security review is part of the Opus review.

decisions_taken.question: Integrated terminal
decisions_taken.decision: Sessions live in the daemon (terminal.* methods and stream) on an in-house ConPTY behind a forge-core PtySpawner trait. The process is assigned to the Job object before it resumes, which is why portable-pty is not used. Admin role, not local_only. terminal.input is deduplicated by input_seq rather than the request_id cache. Output is a 1 MiB byte ring with resume, and terminal.lagged triggers a reset and replay.

decisions_taken.question: Database and mail backends without per-tool Rust code
decisions_taken.decision: Optional manifest blocks: spec.database (protocol family, client runner, SQL templates, dump/restore/shell, url/env) and spec.mail (api family mailpit-v1, port names, env). The daemon runs the declared clients with strict identifier validation. db.shell returns ShellCommandDto, a safe break because it was never implemented. db.export writes .sql.zst through the zstd crate. mail.changed comes from a daemon watcher polling Mailpit /api/v1/info every 3 s while the instance runs. Email HTML is shown in a sandboxed srcdoc iframe with no scripts, no same-origin and remote images blocked. db.open, the Redis section, DB users and scheduled backups move to M3 with notes in docs/07.

decisions_taken.question: Logs
decisions_taken.decision: New logs.targets method. The client merges up to 8 subscriptions. Per-format parsers are selected by the manifest format, never by tool id. There is one access-log parser, in forge-metrics (E5-T3), which the Logs site: target reuses. The LogViewer is shared: E3-T12 delivers it and replaces the minimal Logs tab of the E2 service detail. Every logs.subscribe target uses a single seq domain (E2-T2 fixes the shipped bug first).

decisions_taken.question: Settings and config
decisions_taken.decision: system.config_list returns values, defaults and a JSON Schema, so the Settings screen is generated from the schema. ConfigValueDto.requires lists follow-up actions (e.g. tls.ca_rotate after a TLD change). A config.changed event is added. Config writes are serialized through one owner, which fixes lost read-modify-write updates. Changes are applied live where possible (DNS on/off, re-render on TLD change).

decisions_taken.question: Metrics v1 design
decisions_taken.decision:
- The manifest declares the access-log format as JSON-pointer field mappings plus units, with no per-server parser.
- Logs are tailed by polling every 250 ms with backoff, not notify (docs/14 updated). Daemon rotation per the manifest: nginx rename+reopen, Caddy rolls its own logs, Apache decided by experiment.
- In-memory tiers: 2 s histograms for 10 min, 10 s scalar points for 24 h, 1 min HDR histograms for 24 h.
- SQLite: metrics_1m kept 7 days and metrics_1h kept 90 days, storing HDR V2 blobs with a format_version column. Percentiles always come from merged histograms, never averages.
- CPU attribution: shared pools split by summed upstream time (shown as ≈); dedicated pools and apps are exact; web servers are not attributed.
- New stats.series and stats.routes; TopDto.machine.
- metrics.subscribe sends a snapshot on resume, then every 2/10/60 s depending on the window.
- Per-site metrics on/off and pool_mode are new site columns. Metrics are off by default in portable roots.
- forge-metrics depends only on forge-core.
- oha is installed with `cargo install --root` into the cache.
- The CPU budget is measured with Task Manager normalization, with % of one core also reported.

tasks.title: Frontend state layer: event reducers with rAF batching, entity stores, jobs, capabilities, resync, metrics polling, describeError, reconnect queue
tasks.summary:
src/state is the single data layer for E2, E3 and E5; it merges the E1-T9 and E2-T9 plans. Everything is a projection of DTOs and events, with no domain logic.

Events and stores:
- One events.subscribe per context through the bridge, with a reducer registry covering every EVENT_KINDS entry (each kind is reduced or explicitly ignored), applied in one batch per requestAnimationFrame. Flush on visibilitychange and cap the batch size.
- Zustand stores keyed by ULID: connection (state, hello, RTT), services/pools, sites, tools/updates (tool.updates_available), jobs, system (dns/tls), attention inputs.
- TanStack Query keys per method, with invalidation rules per event (debounced).
- Resync: on {reset}, {lagged} or a reconnect with last_seq below the cursor, refetch the snapshots once.

Jobs: useJob(jobId) follows events, keeps a 1 s jobs.get safety poll, and supports cancel.

Metrics: useMetricsPoll polls services.status every 2 s only while a consumer is mounted, visible and focused. It keeps a 30-sample ring per instance and pool, derives req/s from requests_total deltas, and computes the status-bar totals (daemon cpu/rss + stack). service.metrics events are not used.

Capabilities: useCapabilities combines hello.local, role and not_implemented with METHODS local_only/min_role, and returns a reason key for anything unavailable.

Errors and reconnects:
- describeError(ApiError | FailureReasonDto) gives an i18n cause plus actions, each with its CLI command.
- Reconnect queue: user-triggered mutating calls are held up to 30 s with their request_id.

useJob resolves via events and via the poll when events are dropped; cancel ends in the cancelled state
useMetricsPoll makes 0 calls when hidden or unmounted (fake timers) and resumes within 2 s; req/s from 100→140 over 2 s = 20.0
describeError covers every ERROR_CODES entry and FailureReasonDto kind in pt-BR and en-US, with ≥ 1 action for port_in_use, needs_elevation, not_implemented, unauthorized
Reconnect queue sends after Connected with the same request_id and fails with a localized error after 30 s; capabilities mark local_only methods unavailable when hello.local=false

tasks.title: Fix logs.subscribe sequence domain (backlog vs live, rotation, resume) — CLI regression
tasks.summary:
Today:
- Instance targets number the tail backlog by file line, but live lines by an in-memory LogHub seq starting at 1 per daemon process.
- File targets reset seq to 0 on rotation (follow_file).
- resume_from never replays lines missed while disconnected.
The client drops live lines with seq ≤ last_seq. This also breaks the shipped `forge logs -f`.

Fix: one monotonic seq domain per target. Use the absolute line index across the retained file set, including rotated files, for both backlog and live lines. On resume, replay from the files when the cursor is within the retained data, otherwise send logs.lagged{missed}. Return the true last_seq so clients can detect resets. Keep the follower in spawn_blocking, and keep the existing slow-subscriber behaviour.

The change must be self-contained (logs.rs, the LogHub module, tests) so it can be cherry-picked to a 0.1.x hotfix if the user decides to.

tasks.title: forge-metrics: log tailer (polling, partial lines, rotation, checkpoints, adaptive sampling)
tasks.summary:
One Tailer task per file, ticking every 250 ms with jitter and backing off to 1 s when idle.

Reading: incremental reads in spawn_blocking, ≤ 4 MiB per tick; the partial last line is buffered; std share mode READ|WRITE|DELETE, so server rotation is never blocked.

Rotation: detected by a creation-time change, size < offset, or the file vanishing. The old handle is drained before switching. A missing file is waited for.

Checkpoint {creation_time, offset}: exposed so persistence (T7) can store it in the same transaction as the flush. Resume when the identity matches and the lag is ≤ 64 MiB, else start at EOF with a warning.

Adaptive sampling: when the backlog is > 8 MiB or the cap is hit, parse 1 line in k (k up to 16), scale the counts and mark the bucket sampled. Output goes through a bounded channel, never blocking. No notify, no Win32: std metadata only.
